affoVsNetIncome.title: AFFO vs Statutory Net Income
affoVsNetIncome.content:
AFFO (Adjusted Funds From Operations) strips out non-cash IAS 40 investment-property fair-value movements and equity-accounted associate revaluations, leaving cash distributable earnings after interest, current tax and maintenance capex/incentives. Statutory Net Income keeps the fair-value moves in.

For Stride: NetIncome swung from +$131.9m (FY2021, rising valuations) to -$116.7m (FY2023) and -$56.1m (FY2024) purely on cap-rate and property-value marks, while AFFO moved only modestly across the same years (43.3m to 51.6m to 42.1m). AFFO, not NetIncome, is what funds the dividend.

What to watch:

  • AFFO per security trend (peaked 10.83c FY2021, now 7.60c FY2026)
  • Whether the dividend (8.0c) stays covered by AFFO
  • Do not use NetIncome-based P/E -- it is meaningless here

revenue.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
revenue.content:
Total reported revenue combines SPL's net rental income and SIML's management fee income.

For Stride: Revenue has been roughly flat-to-declining since FY2023 as SPL recycled assets (Silverdale Centre sold to Investore for $114m, Woolworths sites sold) and the office segment softened.

What to watch:

  • Whether asset recycling proceeds are redeployed into higher-yield opportunities
  • SIML fee growth offsetting SPL rental declines

eps.title: Statutory EPS (cents)
eps.content:
Earnings per stapled security, calculated on statutory Net Income -- which is dominated by non-cash property revaluations under IAS 40.

For Stride: EPS swung from -21.6c (FY2023 loss on revaluations) to +32.99c (FY2021 gain on revaluations). This is NOT operating performance; use AFFO per security instead.

What to watch:

  • Direction of cap-rate moves (softening cap rates = valuation losses)
  • Never build a P/E multiple off this series

nta.title: NTA per Security
nta.content:
Net Tangible Assets per stapled security -- the REIT's book-value-per-share anchor, after deducting all liabilities including debt and lease liabilities from total assets.

For Stride: NTA fell from $2.15 (FY2021) to $1.69 (FY2026) on office cap-rate softening (5.9% to 6.2%), a further Investore stake impairment, and dilution from the FY2021-22 equity raises. The securities have traded at a persistent 0.64-0.70x discount to NTA since FY2023, versus 0.95-1.08x in FY2017-21 when the market capitalised SIML's fee platform more richly.

What to watch:

  • Direction of office cap rates (6.2% at FY2026)
  • Price-to-NTA discount narrowing or widening
  • Further associate impairments (Investore carried above its market value)

debt.title: Total Debt & Cash
debt.content:
Bank debt drawn against Stride's facilities, and cash on hand.

For Stride: Net debt of ~$278.6m is recorded for reference only -- it is NEVER subtracted from AFFO, distributable profit or NTA in the valuation, since those flows are already stated after interest and the balance sheet is already net of debt. 95% of drawn debt is fixed at a 5.04% weighted cost; no facility maturities until FY2030 (bank LVR 34%, covenant 50%).

What to watch:

  • Bank LVR trend toward or away from the 50% covenant
  • Refinancing terms as facilities approach FY2030 maturity

propertyEquity.title: Total Assets & Shareholders' Equity
propertyEquity.content:
Total balance-sheet assets (mostly investment property plus equity-accounted associate stakes) against total shareholders' equity.

For Stride: Both have declined since the FY2022 peak (Total Assets $1.64bn to $1.29bn FY2026) as property values were written down and non-core assets recycled to Investore and other buyers.

What to watch:

  • Whether asset-value declines stabilise as cap rates find a floor
  • Equity erosion versus the flat share count

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
Percentage of leasable area under lease across the group's directly-owned portfolio.

For Stride: Group occupancy held at 95% in FY2026, but this blends a much weaker office segment at 85.7% (down from 87.7%) against resilient town-centre and industrial assets. Office is ~78% of SPL's directly-held book by value.

What to watch:

  • Office occupancy specifically, not just the group blend
  • Management guides no material office recovery before H2 CY2027

revenueSplit.title: Gross Rental Income vs Management Fee Income
revenueSplit.content:
The two legs of Stride's stapled model: SPL's gross rental income from directly-owned property, and SIML's external management fee income earned on capital it does not own (~NZ$2.4bn external AUM).

For Stride: Management fee income is capital-light and higher-margin than rental income, and has compounded at 11.6%/yr since FY2017 (8.5m to 22.9m) even though rental income is larger in absolute dollars. It has been roughly flat since FY2021 (25.1m to 22.9m) as Diversified's development activity faded, and faces a dated event risk: the Diversified NZ Property Fund's 10-year mandate review in calendar 2026, which management estimates could cut normalised distributable profit 5-6% if unitholders vote to wind it up.

What to watch:

  • Outcome of the Diversified 10-year review (expected by the FY2027 interim, Nov-2026)
  • Activity-based fee swings from leasing/development/transactions
  • Whether Investore or Industre signal any mandate re-tender

aum.title: Committed AUM
aum.content:
Total committed assets under management across all Products SIML manages, including SPL's own cornerstone stakes.

For Stride: ~NZ$3.3bn committed AUM at FY2026 (~NZ$2.4bn external, i.e. capital SIML earns fees on but does not own). Only disclosed from FY2023 onward in these filings.

What to watch:

  • Growth in external AUM as the direct driver of recurring fee income
  • Development pipeline (North Wharf, Patiki Road) adding to committed AUM over time

dividend.title: Dividend per Security
dividend.content:
Cash dividend paid per stapled security.

For Stride: Cut from 9.91c to 8.0c at FY2023 and held flat since. FY2026's 8.0c dividend was 105% of AFFO (7.60c) and 91% of distributable profit (8.78c) -- uncovered by the company's own owner-earnings measure, funded partly by the gap between distributable profit and AFFO (maintenance capex and incentives).

What to watch:

  • Whether AFFO recovers enough to cover the flat 8.0c guided for FY2027
  • Any further cut if the Diversified mandate is lost and AFFO falls further
